subject: Primary-source map of Coinbase, Circle, Ripple, stablecoin distribution economics, XRP collateral eligibility, custody and regulatory infrastructure.

claims_supported: Q3 2026 net income $719M; adjusted net income $78M; adjusted EBITDA $333M.
Crypto trading volume market share 10.7%, fourth consecutive quarter of gains.
Average USDC held in Coinbase products $22B, up 49% year over year, roughly 30% of average USDC market capitalization.
Coinbase says it captured approximately 50% of USDC economics over the prior year.
Subscription and services revenue was 49% of net revenue; prediction markets exceeded $200M annualized revenue.
limitations: Company-reported financial and operating metrics; read with the 10-Q and non-GAAP reconciliations.

claims_supported: For the quarter ended 2026-09-30, Coinbase says it renewed its arrangement with Circle on the same terms.
The filing provides the regulated-company context for Q3 results and USDC distribution economics.
limitations: The filing does not disclose every commercial term of the private agreement.

claims_supported: Circle reported average USDC in circulation of $76.524B for Q2 2026 and a 3.5% reserve return rate.
Reserve income was 95.2% of Circle total revenue in Q2 2026.
Coinbase receives allocations based on USDC held on its platform after issuer retention and half of the remaining ecosystem-growth amount after approved third-party participants.
Circle reported Coinbase-related distribution costs of $324.6M for Q2 2026 and $655.3M for H1 2026.
Circle Payment Network connects eligible financial institutions for 24/7/365 stablecoin payment settlement.
Circle described Arc testnet/private-mainnet development and planned September 2026 public-mainnet launch as of the filing period.
limitations: Q2 figures are not Q3 results; Circle's Q3 webcast is scheduled after this capture cutoff.
Reserve income and distribution-cost amounts are period-specific and affected by rates and balances.

claims_supported: In August 2023 Circle acquired Coinbase's remaining 50% interest in Centre for approximately 8.4M Circle common shares.
The August 2023 Collaboration Agreement gave Coinbase a minority equity stake in Circle.
Circle pays Coinbase for USDC distribution and ecosystem growth based on reserve income and platform/market balances.
limitations: Historical registration-statement disclosure; current economics should be read with Circle's 2026 10-Q and Coinbase's 2026 10-Q.

claims_supported: Binance was Circle's first approved participant under the Stablecoin Ecosystem Agreement.
Circle disclosed a $60.25M one-time upfront fee and monthly incentives tied to USDC balances.
Binance agreed to keep at least $1.5B of USDC in treasury and, subject to exceptions, to keep $3B.
limitations: Historical contractual disclosure; verify current term, balances and performance before treating as present-day flows.

claims_supported: Coinbase Global Exchange lists XRP among accepted cross-collateral assets alongside USDC and other cryptoassets.
Collateral use is capped by organization-level average daily quantity (ADQ) limits.
Collateral value applies the greater of a base haircut and closeout-horizon haircut.
Collateral may be automatically liquidated if margin coverage falls below maintenance requirements.
limitations: The page does not publish a fixed XRP haircut in the extracted text; limits are account/asset specific.
Global Exchange is a distinct product from Coinbase Prime Global Derivatives and Coinbase U.S. Derivatives.

claims_supported: The Global Derivatives cross-collateral product is available to eligible customers in supported regions outside the U.S.
XRP is listed as a cross-collateral currency.
The displayed XRP haircut is 0% for Cross Portfolio Margin (X:PM) and 15% for Standard Margin (X:SM).
The updated terms apply to most customers from 2026-10-01.
limitations: This is a specific Global Derivatives offering, not Coinbase Prime Global Derivatives or U.S. Derivatives.
Eligibility, account configuration, risk controls and regional restrictions apply.

source_registry.capture_method: official Coinbase Prime help page extract
claims_supported: Coinbase Prime Global Derivatives lists USDC, BTC and ETH as eligible collateral/settlement assets.
USD must be converted to USDC in Prime first.
The page says U.S. Derivatives on Coinbase Derivatives Exchange use USD cash only.
Cross-collateral between settlement currencies is not enabled in this Prime Global Derivatives portfolio.
limitations: This product-specific list does not negate XRP support on Coinbase Global Exchange or Coinbase Advanced Global Derivatives.

claims_supported: Coinbase's crypto-backed USDC loans use Morpho on Base.
XRP is listed among eligible collateral assets.
Eligibility is limited by region, including U.S. customers excluding New York and limited UK/Canada access.
Coinbase says loan proceeds cannot be used for trading on Coinbase.
limitations: This is a DeFi-backed loan product with protocol/liquidity/security risks; it is not an exchange margin or institutional derivatives collateral program.

claims_supported: RLUSD became available on Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange and the Coinbase app on 2026-10-28.
Deposits and withdrawals are supported on XRPL, Base and Ethereum.
Coinbase says Global Exchange availability and RLUSD collateral use would follow, not be available at initial launch.
Ripple would provide liquidity on Base.
limitations: The launch announcement does not establish current Global Exchange collateral activation or actual volumes.

claims_supported: Ripple and Coinbase announced RLUSD distribution on Coinbase retail, Exchange and Prime.
RLUSD can move across XRPL, Base and Ethereum.
The announcement said Global Exchange collateral availability would follow.
Ripple described RLUSD market capitalization as more than $2.4B in this release.
limitations: Counterparty press release; $2.4B is the release's dated company-reported figure, not a current independent market-cap snapshot.

claims_supported: Ripple said it was on track to exit 2026 with a $900M annualized product revenue run rate.
Ripple reported over $16T in transactions enabled across its products in 2025, 1,700+ institutional/corporate/enterprise customers and over 85 licenses.
Ripple reported RLUSD market capitalization at $2.6B in this separate release.
Ripple announced multi-solution relationships involving BNY, DriveWealth, Robinhood, Water.org and other partners.
Ripple and BNY described a tokenized trade-finance initiative on XRPL with C2FO.
limitations: Company-reported figures and forward-looking run-rate; not independently audited in this release.
The $2.6B RLUSD figure differs from the $2.4B figure in Ripple's same-day Coinbase listing release; preserve as dated source disagreement.

claims_supported: Standard Chartered's institutional custody support for RLUSD issued on XRPL is live through its DIFC branch regulated by DFSA.
Standard Chartered, Ripple and LMAX are working toward RLUSD as eligible collateral for agreed LMAX products.
The collateral-mirroring model is intended to avoid transferring RLUSD directly to the trading venue.
limitations: Collateral integration remains planned and subject to final documentation, testing, applicable law, internal approvals and jurisdiction readiness.

claims_supported: Ripple announced final OCC approval for Ripple National Trust Bank on 2026-10-26.
The approved activities include management of segregated RLUSD reserves, acting as collateral trustee for RLUSD reserves and fiduciary digital-asset custody.
Ripple says RLUSD remains issued by Standard Custody & Trust Company, its NYDFS-regulated limited-purpose trust company.
limitations: Final charter approval is not proof that the bank has opened or begun every approved activity; Ripple says custody services are available upon opening.

source_registry.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
claims_supported: OCC record identifies Ripple National Trust Bank, charter application 2025-Charter-342347.
The OCC record shows initial approval on 2025-12-12 and consummated/effective date 2026-10-26.
limitations: The record is a charter status page; operational launch and activity commencement require separate evidence.

claims_supported: Circle scheduled its Q3 2026 results webcast for 2026-11-04 at 08:00 ET / 13:00 UTC.
limitations: Scheduled event only; Q3 results had not been captured at this artifact cutoff.

relationships.notes: Coinbase receives economics tied to USDC held on its platform and broader ecosystem growth; Coinbase also has a minority equity stake in Circle. This is a material commercial/equity relationship.
Historical agreement included upfront and balance-based incentives; current performance and balances need fresh confirmation.
ADQ limits and haircuts apply; do not generalize to every Coinbase derivatives product.
0% X:PM and 15% X:SM haircut shown; regional and account eligibility apply.
The cited Prime portfolio accepts USDC/BTC/ETH; this is distinct from Global Exchange and Coinbase Advanced Global Derivatives.
On Base through Morpho; not a Coinbase derivatives margin product.
RLUSD retail/Exchange/Prime availability on XRPL, Base and Ethereum; Global Exchange collateral was future at launch.
Custody through SC DIFC branch; not evidence of XRP custody.
Future collateral eligibility remains subject to documentation, testing, approvals and jurisdiction readiness.
Approved activities include RLUSD reserve management, collateral trusteeship and fiduciary custody; bank opening/operations are separate milestones.

relationships.type: tokenized trade-finance collaboration on XRPL with C2FO
relationships.notes: Ripple company announcement; implementation and volumes need separate evidence.

product_scope_matrix.limits: Eligibility varies by region; U.S. excludes New York; limited UK/Canada access.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase product support may increase the utility of XRP as collateral, but the market effect depends on actual pledged balances, limits and utilization.
support: XRP is accepted on Global Exchange cross collateral, eligible non-US Global Derivatives and Morpho-backed USDC loans.
disconfirming_or_missing: No actual XRP collateral balances, utilization, haircut utilization, liquidation or borrowing volumes are disclosed in the cited help pages.
tests: Seek product-level collateral utilization, ADQ limits, XRP balances and loan origination/repayment data.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase's large USDC balances and Circle revenue-sharing agreement create material economic interdependence that may shape stablecoin distribution and payment-rail competition.
support: Circle 10-Q specifies the allocation formula and costs; Coinbase reports $22B average USDC balances and about 50% of USDC economics.
disconfirming_or_missing: Q3 Circle results were not yet released at capture; actual net economics depend on reserve rates, third-party incentives and platform balances.
tests: Ingest Circle Q3 filing after release; reconcile Coinbase Q3 filing and Circle Q3 distribution costs.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase distribution plus Standard Chartered custody and planned LMAX collateral could broaden RLUSD institutional utility, but initial Coinbase Global Exchange collateral was not live at launch.
support: Coinbase/Ripple announced retail, Exchange and Prime access; Standard Chartered custody is live on XRPL; LMAX collateral integration is planned.
disconfirming_or_missing: No verified Global Exchange RLUSD collateral activation, LMAX product eligibility or cross-venue RLUSD settlement volume.
tests: Monitor Coinbase product status, LMAX documentation and issuer/attestation data.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Ripple's final OCC charter approval may strengthen RLUSD reserve governance and custody, but actual operational capabilities begin only when the trust bank opens and activates approved services.
support: OCC record shows effective date 2026-10-26; Ripple says activities will be provided upon opening.
disconfirming_or_missing: No opening notice or first transaction/custody evidence in this capture.
tests: Track OCC filings, bank opening notices, reserve custody disclosures and service commencement.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Stablecoin growth and XRP collateral eligibility are related infrastructure signals but do not establish direct XRP spot demand.
support: Coinbase and Circle economics are primarily USDC reserve/distribution; Ripple's RLUSD is a separate USD stablecoin; XRP is a distinct volatile asset.
disconfirming_or_missing: Actual collateral balances and settlement conversion flows are not disclosed.
tests: Separate stablecoin supply/settlement from XRP inventory, collateral pledges, exchange flows and executed trades.

source_independence_notes: Coinbase and Circle SEC filings are counterpart disclosures from related commercial parties; compare both, but do not count them as independent market demand.
Coinbase and Ripple jointly announced RLUSD listing; each is a party to the relationship.
Ripple's regulatory announcement is cross-checked against OCC's Corporate Applications Search record.
Product-help pages establish eligibility, not actual collateral utilization or balance-sheet exposure.

Current RLUSD balances and volume by Coinbase product, chain and custody location.
Current LMAX collateral implementation status and Standard Chartered custody balances.
Ripple National Trust Bank opening/operational commencement evidence.
Current SEC/issuer disclosures on Coinbase/Circle shareholding and contractual amendments beyond disclosed summaries.
quarantined: Coinbase Q3 metrics as evidence of XRP demand.
RLUSD market-cap figures from two same-day Ripple releases until timestamp/methodology reconciled.
Planned LMAX collateral integration as if already live.
Ripple National Trust Bank final charter approval as if all operations are already active.
XRP collateral eligibility as if it means XRP is accepted across every Coinbase derivatives product.

predictions.reason: These corporate and product disclosures establish infrastructure and eligibility, not synchronized XRP demand or predictive features. No directional forecast is supported.
